The kernel provides the Adreno GPU through KGSL at `/dev/kgsl-3d0`. It provides the system DMA heap at `/dev/dma_heap/system`. `system/plasma.config` binds both devices into the container. `rungic-plasma` writes device rules from their current device numbers.

Linux consumers include Mesa's freedreno KGSL backend, libcamera and ksystemstats. Mesa supports KWin, Xwayland, Flatpak's GL extension and GL/Vulkan programs. Consumers open the GPU read-write and the heap read-only. The container grants only read access to the heap. Libcamera uses the `dmabuf-system-heap-read-only` patch.

The provider check reads device types and permissions as the desktop user. It also uses `rungic-gpu-probe` to render a 64x64 picture offscreen through KGSL, GBM, EGL and GLES. The check shows no picture on the screen. A PC uses DRM's render node instead.

The consumer check has a gap recorded in `quality/interfaces.yaml`. KGSL is Qualcomm's kernel interface. No substitute is available outside the phone.
